canonical_check.why: The reality check (2026-09-15) re-measures every quantity the audit (2026-09-14) reports, on the refetched corpus of 19,581 images instead of 11,349, and says measurements outrank the morning report; its box rate (17.3% vs 29%), caption-held-out numbers (37.9%/57.1% vs 38.3%/56.8%), modality reading (49% not an x-ray vs detector miss) and Castellvi strata replace the audit's. The audit keeps content the reality check does not repeat (per-level recall, hardware constraints, renderer fixes, the 400-panel read plan), so it is superseded for its numbers, not deleted as a source.

The reality check explicitly supersedes the overnight report's counts (19,048 images, 1,489 refetched, 927 video panels) and says measurements outrank the morning report, so the overnight report is canonical only for what the reality check does not cover; but its 08:30 update postdates the reality check's 06:55 to 07:15 snapshot on the v2 model (registered 08:13, 64.2% on 800 renders) and on the CUT v2 job ids, so on those two items the overnight report is the later record. A superseded relation from overnight-report to reality-check, with the v2 items excepted, fits the records better than two canonical pages.

The card is a frozen 2026-09-14 09:43 view (10,281 rows, dataset 0.2) whose counts, figure-mate number (88%) and provenance sentence are contradicted the same day by the audit and superseded by the reality check (17,486 rows) and the atlas (21,603 rows, 29,500 panels); its licence tiers and release framing conflict with the later private-forever rule. It stays canonical for the licence tiers, inclusion and exclusion rules and the reader protocol, not for counts or release intent.

No later page redraws the pipeline, so the map remains the one description of the routes; its counts (197k frames, manifest v0.3) and its network and serving invariants are dated or contradicted (the access setup's grid plan, the lab recipe's 121 MB of shipped weights, the handoff's anchor_drr leak), so a reader takes its structure and not its numbers.

found.unsourced_summary: The dataset card and the pipeline map both assert that the manifest regenerates byte-identical from the same inputs and that an unbroken SHA-256 chain runs from original figure to weights, naming no command, run or checksum file. The map asserts that the grid's outbound IP is captcha-throttled by PMC while WSL is not, and the access setup asserts that publishers authenticate by IP from the university's address space; neither cites a probe, and the overnight report shows the refetch ran through the proxy session instead. The access setup asserts that video frames are the only 1080 px native source and that Instagram serves posts at 1080 px wide, with no measurement; the reality check says the YouTube panels came capped at 720p. The map's anchor panel asserts that an author's printed label is the strongest anchor there is, with no accuracy measured for printed labels, while the reality check says the caption's label was mostly assigned by counting on a limited field. The atlas and the registry both state that 72.8 percent of the 29,500 panels are reproductions with no pixel residual, naming no duplicate-detection run or threshold. The card's 88% figure-mate number carries no pair count. Lift Before Label asserts the renderer is already at the DeepDRR/SyntheX level with no test, and its own adversarial pass never ran. The adjudication bench asserts that the reader's single read is the only ground truth the panel will ever have, and the level verification bench assumes a whole-run-correct panel is the common case; neither assumption is measured, and the card's protocol promises two blind readers with a third adjudicating. The reality check's claims that 'Castellvi I is two thirds of transitional anatomy' and that registration-derived labels are biased are stated without a source in the records.
found.stale_summary: All six primary pages are snapshots of 14 to 15 September 2026 with running work inside them: the card says dataset version 0.2 with 0.3 in progress and reader labels pending for every panel; the pipeline map draws manifest v0.3 and 197k YouTube frames; the access setup says the PMC refetch is running now and worries about a library note of 30 June 2026; the overnight report says round two of the refetch is still running, the FluoroGen array was cancelled at 05:50, the CUT v2 is queued as jobs 40285316/7 and the v2 retrain registered at 08:13; the reality check, read between 06:55 and 07:15, says the v2 weights were destroyed and retrain 40285209 is pending, lists CUT jobs 40285274 and 40285275 as queued, and lays out a 90-day and 12-month plan from 15 September. The lab recipe of 2026-09-27 says the website shipped weights until 2026-09-14. canonical_check.why: Both are WSU eProtocol drafts of 'Protocol 1' for the retrospective fluoroscopy collection, mirroring IRB-21-10-4123. The retrospective protocol is the later text: it cites the 2 September 2026 determination 2026_269, the 16 October 2026 AIDaS deadline and a January 2027 start, where the other is dated 15 September 2026 and says 'Unfunded / departmental'. Neither record could confirm the order from its own text, but the dates and the AIDaS grant's 'builds-on' relation settle it. Caveat: the later draft is a redesign rather than a revision: Expedited 5 instead of Exempt 4, one surgeon's 2021-2026 cases instead of 40,000 studies from 2006, detector recall from operative-note truth instead of CT-registered labels, and the fracture-detection and registry-linkage aims, the 6,000-vertebrae stratified target and the 'Protocol 2 submitted alongside' line are dropped, not carried. The two also come from different accounts. So 'superseded' holds for the submission, but the older draft's aims are abandoned, and downstream notes (lift-before-label) still expect its registered frames.

found.unsourced_summary: The cluster's business case is held up by figures no artifact sources. The proposal (counting-levels-under-fluoroscopy), the seed grant (aidas-seed-grant-proposal) and the protocol (retrospective-fluoroscopy-protocol) all say every radiation-safety prerequisite takes fifteen business days, with no WSU page cited. The proposal and the grant assume the DMC PACS holds every saved fluoroscopic series of one surgeon's spine cases for 2021-2026 with operative notes and post-operative imaging for truth, while the older eProtocol draft and the fluorocap note cite another centre where half the cases were off PACS and the protocol's frames-per-case waits on a 20-case pilot. The proposal says cadaver work needs no IRB, the grant leaves phantom IACUC/RSC open, and the cadaver fee ($1,000-3,000) and the GPU, Jetson, grabber and phantom prices are list estimates with no quotes. The ten operating-room minutes saved per case (proposal) rest on two small non-randomised thoracic series that the visual abstract itself calls the weakest input, inflated by an unexplained 1.35 to 2026 dollars. The navigation comparison in the abstract, the grant and the protocol states that no study shows navigation reduces wrong-level surgery and that no verified capital cost exists, and the abstract's $1.5M over seven years plus 10% service is declared an assumption. Joint Commission 2024 (127, 9, 7, 36%) and NHS England (185) are cited by organisation name only in the grant, the protocol and the abstract; the proposal's registry figures carry no inline citation at all. The protocol's reason for Expedited 5, that research supporting an FDA submission cannot be exempt, and its line that the WSU form limits review to Exempt 2 and 3, cite no regulation; its sentence that synthetic fluoroscopy is tuned to one C-arm and one population is an inference from DeepFluoro alone; its expectation that a full count is possible on only a minority of archived cases is marked to confirm. The older draft's statements that no public intraoperative fluoroscopy with level labels exists (contradicted by the atlas) and that most spine-surgery patients have a pre- or post-operative CT have no source. Among the secondary notes, vertebral-levels-without-ct gives every literature figure without a citation and says 'fixing it took naming from 67% to 92%' with no run named, counting-from-the-sacrum says the 28-point sim-to-real tax 'matches what the field reports elsewhere almost exactly' without the field's numbers, and the OR-readiness ledger's 97% counting-grade threshold is a chosen line, not a derived one.

The seed grant (aidas-seed-grant-proposal) was due October 16, 2026, now past, with the submission address, PI, case count and the $24/h rate still '[to confirm]', biosketches undrafted, refiner results 'pending' that the proposal already tabled, and a manuscript 'in preparation' that the 8 October handoff says is held pending the technology-transfer office, with the disclosure filed 2026-09-25 and no provisional recorded. The retrospective protocol is 'Date Submitted: Draft', expects AIDaS notification December 16, 2026 and a January 2027 start, and leaves frames per case and the verification fraction to a 20-case pilot; the older eProtocol draft of 15 September 2026 carries '40,000 studies — unconfirmed', '7 years — confirm', citations to insert and a pending trauma co-investigator. Neither protocol nor the grant mentions the HPR 2026-330 supplement of 29 September that the atlas records, and the atlas (17 October) still asks whether DUA data needs its own determination. The atlas lists eleven unsent Outlook drafts and an unconfirmed USD 250 Radiopaedia fee; the grid note says the Radiopaedia licence waits on countersignature and JHU had not replied on 21 October; the handoff of 8 October had the cine-source letters 'drafted; none sent'. The research-directions note (8 October) counts zero verified transitional real-frame test persons against 35 needed, while vertebral-levels-without-ct (18 September) had a 376-patient transitional cross-validation 'running now'; counting-from-the-sacrum and what-is-left-after-physics (22 September) describe training and measurements in progress whose results no cluster artifact reports. The lab recipe notes the public mirror still at v10 on 2026-09-27 and weights shipped on the website until 2026-09-14. The outreach note read funder pages in September 2026 and expects RSNA cycles to open in October. The lift-before-label note's verification pass never ran and it still expects registered frames from the older Protocol 1 design; the fluorocap note has the PACS capture object type undetermined and FluoroCap QC pending on all 21,603 rows.
